A lens with `standards: false` keys no standards text, only their source and trust, so turning a lens's standards off asks its runs again once, by [the decision of 2026-11-19](../decisions/2026-11-19-lenses-get-only-the-standards-they-cite.md). As a lens record's key, it lets `melian records relay` take a lens run's early copy, with no check, beside a round that reads a lens record under the same key, by [issue #397](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/397). For a run that probes, it holds the probing wording its planner and prober read: the shared lines, and the entries in core's `lensProbingWording` of its lens's `probesAs`, or of its own name. So a change to one lens's words asks no other lens's run again. [Issue #493](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/493) changed the trust-boundary lens's probing wording on purpose, so its probing runs are asked again once. For a run that escalates to another, it holds the shared lines, which carry its findings on, by rule 8 and [the per-lens wording decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md). For a run offered `list_mutants`, the key holds the instrumenter that answers it, `@stryker-mutator/instrumenter`, by [the decision of 2026-11-16](../decisions/2026-11-16-lens-request-keys-the-mutant-instrumenter.md). It holds its version, read from the `package.json` of the package the tool resolves. It holds its source, the checkout's install or Melian's, or `unavailable` when neither resolves. A run not offered the tool keys nothing more. A probing run's environment names its host by one value, `probingHost`, whose architecture and Node version come from core's `hostFacts`: the sandbox's platform and kind, the installed sandbox-runtime release, read from its own `package.json`, and the CPU architecture and version of the Node that runs the probe. Left out of that value: the operating system's release, since the platform names the system; the CPU's model, since the architecture names the instruction set Node runs; whether the filesystem folds case, since a probing run is reused only from its own checkout's store, so a temporary directory moved to a volume that folds differently copies a run probed under the other rule; and the host's locale and clock, which no probe should hang on. Left out of the request, by [the probing reuse decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md): what Melian's probe runner gives a probe and what `run_probe` returns, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437), so a release that changes them copies a run probed under the old code; and what the read paths hold, the installed dependencies of the code under test among them, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, so a reinstall between two reviews of one head copies the run and its conclusive reruns. A task stored before the key, lens task version 6, holds no request key, so nothing is copied from it and the first review after the upgrade runs every lens once. The lens tools' own code, `list_mutants`'s included, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-15: the text each tool returns to the model, what each tool does, and the lens extension's code, which the key cannot hold as data. Rule 8 forbids hashing source at run time, so [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) ties a code version to a hash of them in a test; until then a change there reuses runs asked under the old code. The packages beneath the instrumenter, such as Babel, which a reinstall can move while the instrumenter's version stays the same, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, [as recorded on pull request #492](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/492#issuecomment-6907598594). A level where they may not, whose prober's tier the plan refuses, or whose prober's tier has no route, runs as it would without `probe`, and the lens's record carries a note that says `<level> ran without probes` and why. Under `requireProbes`, which `melian review --require-probes` sets, such a level fails instead. Before the lens runs, the review checks the level it selected and, for `quick`, the level it may escalate to. The lens records `failed` at the first that cannot probe, runs at neither, and `probeGap` receives the level and its cause. A settled run whose prober asked for a probe that could not run fails the same way, its escalated run's first included. So does one with an attack whose every probe `probeConclusive` rejects, unless the prober skipped that attack, with the cause `probe-inconclusive`. Triage's levels and questions do not change. Each candidate whose claims a probing run reported carries `probes` by `claimKey` and the run's `probing`. Before it starts verification, the review runs each claim's probe again under the harness's sandbox and stores the run in the root's `ProbeReruns` by revision and `rerunKey`, unless a conclusive run is stored already: one that was refused, timed out, was cut or was ended by a signal runs again. `rerunKey` names the probe by its tool task, so a review that reuses the run, by attaching to its task or copying it, finds the stored run, and a new run never does. A review whose lens task another has replaced, before its reruns or while they run, fails as superseded there. The verification task, from version 4, reads those runs in its spawn commit, gives the verifier `boundProbeEvidence`, and records in each claim's policy whether its probe failed again. `boundProbeEvidence` renders each claim's evidence with `renderProbeEvidence` and, when the candidate's blocks together pass `probeEvidenceBudget`, 128 KiB in UTF-8 bytes, cuts every part a model or the head wrote to the largest common size that fits, keeping both ends. The plan is cut as two parts, the attacks before and after the one the probe answered, whose row stays whole. A cut claim's block adds a note from `probeEvidenceCutWording` outside the boundary, naming each cut part and its bytes, files by number, and the rule for judging cut evidence. Evidence that passes the budget with every part cut to nothing renders as `undefined`. The spawn commit then creates no conversation for that candidate, and its verify phase answers `unanswered` with a reason that names the budget and the count of probing claims, so the review reads not reviewed. The verifier's version does not hash that table. `verificationRequest` keys, in `cuts`, the evidence each cut candidate is shown, from the `boundProbeEvidence` call the prompt makes. It cuts under the review's nonce, since quoting replaces that nonce in the head's text and so changes its size, then names the boundary by a fixed nonce. A refused candidate keys the reason it is asked nothing. The candidate's probes and `ProbeReruns` keep every byte. Version 6 lets each model of a candidate's route name its own thinking level, so a build that knows version 5 alone leaves the task unrun; `test/fixtures/verification-v4-main/` reopens main's version 4, and `test/fixtures/verification-v5-481/` the version 5 that names each shown dismissal's record.

A later import never rebuilds a record the store holds, so it never changes the ID, and only a dismissal replaced since asks the verifier again. The review lists its store once, and verification and export both read that listing, so the ID the request names is the ID the round exports. So are the probe reruns the verifier is shown, the empty value when there are none, and each probe evidence block with the wording it is rendered from, its lens's judgement included. A verification that holds a claim resting on a probe also holds `judges`, the judgement of each lens whose claims rest on one, keyed by the built-in whose wording that lens reads. So a change to one lens's judgement asks again only the verifications of that lens's probed claims. So is, in `cuts` by candidate key, the probe evidence each cut candidate's verifier is shown, rendered by the call the prompt makes under the review's nonce, with the boundary then named by a fixed one, or the reason a candidate no cut fits is asked nothing. A request whose evidence all fits holds no `cuts`, so its key is the one it had before cuts. The probe environment each probe evidence block shows holds the installed sandbox-runtime release. A verification with no such claim keys as it did before [the per-lens wording decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md), except for the two failover wordings, which moved every verification's key once, so each stored verification is asked once more after that upgrade, by [the decision of 2026-11-18](../decisions/2026-11-18-failover-wording-in-the-verification-key.md). The code that handles the answer, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) |
